plan.title: Two-Step Wooden Step Stool
plan.summary: A compact two-step stool with warm-finished wooden treads and dark, stair-profile side supports, based on the attached photo. Approximate finished size: 450 mm wide × 500 mm deep × 400 mm high.
assumptions: Dimensions are estimated from the photo because no target dimensions or scale reference were provided.
The front of the stool is z=0; the lower tread is at the front and the higher tread is at the rear.
The two side supports are 18 mm birch plywood with a stair-step outline. Their bottom edges rest directly on the floor.
Treads are 25 mm thick hardwood panels, supported along their edges by the side supports. Slightly ease exposed edges after cutting; this edge rounding is not represented in the geometry.
Balanced-material interpretation: birch plywood supports and poplar or similar hardwood treads. Dark paint on supports and a warm-toned clear finish on treads approximate the photo.
This is a step stool for normal household use, not a ladder or a platform intended for standing on the highest edge.

parts.name: Stair-profile side support
parts.notes: Profile coordinates use z as the 500 mm long axis and y as the 400 mm middle axis. Lower tread support ledge is at y=155 mm; rear upper tread support ledge is at y=375 mm. Supports extend to the floor at y=0.

parts.name: Lower front tread
parts.notes: Rests on the lower horizontal ledges of both side supports. Finished tread top is at y=180 mm.

parts.name: Upper rear tread
parts.notes: Rests on the upper horizontal ledges of both side supports. Finished tread top is at y=400 mm.

consumables.name: Wood glue
consumables.note: For tread-to-support joints.

consumables.name: Black paint or enamel
consumables.note: For the plywood side supports; prime plywood edges as needed.

consumables.name: Warm-toned wood stain
consumables.note: Optional, to approximate the warm tread color in the photo.

consumables.name: Clear water-based polyurethane
consumables.note: Protective finish for treads; apply over stain if used.

consumables.name: Sandpaper
consumables.note: For shaping, smoothing, and finish preparation.

fasteners.name: Slotted steel angle bracket
fasteners.size: 25 x 25 x 40 mm; front-to-back tread slot; support leg with two screw holes

joints.drive_from: Attach brackets to the inside face of each P1 before placing P2; drive the tread screws upward from below through the front-to-back slots.
joints.note: Use two brackets per side contact, about 50 mm from the ends of the ledge. Drive four #8 x 16 mm screws into the P1 plywood face and two #8 x 20 mm pan-head screws with 12 mm flat washers into P2. Verify the pan heads and washers retain the brackets without wedging into the slots; leave the tread screws just loose enough for the brackets to slide. The 20 mm screws provide adequate tread engagement while leaving at least 3 mm below the top face. No glue.

fasteners.name: Slotted steel angle bracket
fasteners.size: 25 x 25 x 40 mm; front-to-back tread slot; support leg with two screw holes

joints.drive_from: Attach brackets to the inside face of each P1 before placing P3; drive the tread screws upward from below through the front-to-back slots.
joints.note: Use two brackets per side contact, about 50 mm from the ends of the ledge. Drive four #8 x 16 mm screws into the P1 plywood face and two #8 x 20 mm pan-head screws with 12 mm flat washers into P3. Verify the pan heads and washers retain the brackets without wedging into the slots; leave the tread screws just loose enough for the brackets to slide. The 20 mm screws provide adequate tread engagement while leaving at least 3 mm below the top face. No glue.

steps.title: Mark and check the parts
steps.text: Use the supplied profile dimensions to mark two matching stair-shaped outlines on P1 stock. Check that P2 and P3 are the specified 450 x 250 mm treads, and label their front and rear edges before cutting or assembly.
steps.tip: Label the inside faces of the supports so the brackets will face inward.

steps.title: Cut the side supports
steps.text: Cut both P1 outlines with a jigsaw, staying just outside the lines, then smooth each cut back to the line. Compare the supports and trim them until their profiles match exactly.
steps.safety: Wear safety glasses and hearing protection; clamp the plywood securely and keep hands clear of the blade.
steps.tip: Support the offcut so it cannot pinch the blade near the end of a cut.

steps.title: Ease and sand the edges
steps.text: Ease the exposed edges of P1, P2, and P3 slightly, then sand all faces and edges with 80, 120, and 180 grit. Keep the support ledges flat so the treads sit evenly.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask and eye protection; connect dust extraction or work in a well-ventilated area.
steps.tip: Do not round over the flat ledges where the treads bear.

steps.title: Dry-fit and mark the assembly
steps.text: Stand the two P1 supports parallel, with their inside faces toward one another, and place P2 and P3 on their matching ledges. Confirm the treads sit flush and the supports are parallel. Mark the bracket locations about 50 mm from the ledge ends and mark the rear-brace location below P3.
steps.tip: Use a square to check that both treads are at right angles to the supports.

steps.title: Drill bracket pilot holes
steps.text: Use each bracket as a template and drill 2.5 mm pilot holes in the support faces and tread undersides. For the tread slots, use the selected #8 x 20 mm pan-head screws and 12 mm flat washers; check that the washer retains the bracket without wedging in its slot. Stop the tread pilots short of the top face.
steps.safety: Clamp the parts before drilling, wear eye protection, and keep the drill bit clear of your hands and the bench.
steps.tip: Mark the drill bit depth so no pilot hole breaks through a visible face.

steps.title: Finish the separate parts
steps.text: Paint P1 dark and apply the optional warm stain to P2 and P3. Apply two or more thin coats of water-based polyurethane to the treads, following the product label. Allow about 2 hours between coats and at least 24 hours before assembly, or longer if the label requires it.
steps.safety: Ventilate the work area, wear gloves and eye protection, and follow finish-label precautions; keep finishes away from flames.
steps.tip: Keep paint and finish out of the bracket pilot holes so the screws seat cleanly.

steps.title: Build and square the rear shear brace
steps.text: Use separately sourced 18 mm birch plywood for a rear shear panel approximately 414 mm wide by 300 mm high, and solid-wood cleats approximately 30 x 30 x 300 mm. Position the panel between the P1 supports at the rear, below P3; glue and screw each cleat to the inside face of a support with three #8 x 38 mm screws spaced along its height. Clamp the frame square, then drive four #8 x 38 mm screws through each panel face into its cleat, with no glue on the panel-to-cleat interface.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection, clamp the supports and brace securely before drilling, and keep hands clear of the drill bit. Support the assembly during lifting.
steps.tip: Predrill the cleats and panel; check that the panel fits between the supports and does not obstruct P3 or the floor.

steps.title: Attach the lower tread
steps.text: With the braced supports held parallel, place two 25 x 25 x 40 mm slotted angle brackets at each P1–P2 contact. Drive four #8 x 16 mm screws from the inside face of each support into its two brackets. From below, install two #8 x 20 mm pan-head screws with 12 mm flat washers through the front-to-back slots into P2; verify the heads and washers retain the brackets without wedging the slots, and do not glue.
steps.safety: Keep the stool stable on padded supports while driving screws, and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Check that both tread-slot screws can move the bracket along its slot before finishing assembly.

steps.title: Attach the upper tread
steps.text: Place P3 on the upper ledges and fit two 25 x 25 x 40 mm slotted angle brackets at each P1–P3 contact. Drive four #8 x 16 mm screws from the inside face of each support into its two brackets. From below, install two #8 x 20 mm pan-head screws with 12 mm flat washers through the front-to-back slots into P3; verify the heads and washers retain the brackets without wedging the slots, and do not glue.
steps.safety: Support the assembly securely before drilling, and keep hands away from the driver bit.
steps.tip: Check that P3 is square to both supports before tightening the bracket screws.

steps.title: Check the assembled stool
steps.text: Check that both supports sit flat, the rear panel and cleats are secure, and the stool does not rock on a level floor. Confirm every tread bracket has four screws into its support and two pan-head screws with flat washers into its tread. Check that the washer-and-head assemblies retain the brackets but do not wedge or lock the slots.
steps.safety: Do not sit or stand on the stool while checking it; keep it on a level floor.
steps.tip: Do not tighten a tread screw so far that its washer clamps the bracket and prevents seasonal movement.

steps.title: Touch up and let the finish cure
steps.text: Touch up any assembly marks with the matching paint or clear finish. Let the finish cure for the time stated on its label—often several days—before household use.
steps.safety: Use ventilation and the finish label’s protective equipment guidance while touching up.

review.summary: The treads have direct bearing on the plywood supports, and the slotted attachments address seasonal movement. However, this load-bearing stool needs transverse bracing, a more precise fastener specification, and clearer assembly positioning before it is ready to build.

issues.problem: There is no transverse brace or shear panel connecting the side supports. Resistance to side-to-side racking depends entirely on small angle brackets, short screws, and tread screws intentionally left free to slide. These attachments are not a dependable substitute for bracing on a stool subjected to shifting body weight.
issues.fix: Add a substantial rear plywood shear panel between the P1 supports below P3. Connect it through vertical solid-wood corner cleats: glue and screw the cleats to the inside faces of P1, then screw through the panel face into the cleats. Use multiple spaced fasteners along each connection, rather than screws into plywood edges. Add the panel, cleats, fasteners, and joints to the plan, and assemble this braced frame square before attaching the treads. Keep P2 and P3 attached without glue through their movement slots.

issues.problem: The generic '#8 x 16 mm wood screws' specification does not establish a suitable head for the tread slots. A countersunk head can wedge into a slot and prevent movement; an undersized head can pull through it. Leaving an unsuitable screw loose does not make a reliable sliding attachment.
issues.fix: Specify pan-head screws with suitable flat washers, or washer-head screws explicitly compatible with the selected brackets. Specify a bracket whose tread slot runs front-to-back and whose support leg accepts two screws. Confirm screw-head clearance and adequate thread engagement with the actual bracket and washer thickness. Update J1, J2, the hardware list, and steps 7–9 to require the head to retain the bracket without wedging into or locking the slot.

issues.problem: Steps 7 and 8 say to drive screws 'from the inside face of each support into each bracket,' which reverses the intended fastening direction. They also do not explicitly follow the joints array's instruction to mount the brackets before placing the treads. With P2 close to the floor, an upright assembly does not provide dependable straight-line driver clearance underneath it.
issues.fix: After finishing, attach the brackets to the separate P1 supports by driving screws through the bracket holes into the plywood faces. Then assemble and brace the supports. For the tread screws, explicitly lay the assembly securely on its side on padded supports, with the underside accessible and at least approximately 150 mm of straight driver clearance. Clamp each tread against its ledges before driving upward through its bracket slots.

issues.problem: The consumables list says the wood glue is for tread-to-support joints, while J1, J2, and the assembly steps correctly prohibit glue there. Following the consumables note would defeat the intended wood-movement allowance.
issues.fix: Remove the tread-to-support glue instruction. If glue is retained for the added bracing, identify those specific joints as its intended use and explicitly state that neither tread is glued to P1.

Frame is 25 x 25 x 2 mm square steel tube. Box placements show the tube's outside dimensions; hollow interiors are not modeled. Have the straight-cut frame professionally welded and powder-coated. This keeps the geometry close to the photo without requiring a home tube bender.

For an all-wood alternative, use a commercially available school chair-desk frame or build a bolted frame from 38 x 38 mm hardwood; the latter will look less like the photo and needs revised geometry.
Seat and back are flat 18 mm plywood with rounded corners, painted red. This approximates the photo's formed seat and back; use purchased molded school-chair shells for a closer fit.
Writing tablet is 18 mm plywood with dark brown stain and clear coat to approximate the woodgrain top.

steps.title: Drill clearance holes and countersinks

steps.safety: Use finishes in strong ventilation with gloves and eye protection, away from flames. Follow the product labels for solvent precautions and disposal.
steps.tip: Test the stain on scrap first, and do not let a thick finish coat narrow the clearance holes.

steps.title: Attach the chair back

steps.safety: Support and clamp P7 so it cannot slip while fastening.

steps.safety: Support the frame and panels while positioning them; keep fingers clear of pinch points.

steps.tip: Common mistake: overtightening screws into plywood. Heads should be flush and secure, not driven deeply into the face.
